decisions.reason: Submitting a developer project-verification request to remediate a false scam warning does not change how fiat buyers access commissions, prizes, tickets, or dashboards.
The trust-verification submission does not change the deferred background wallet-provisioning behavior or any of its wallet-creation rules.
The project-verification request is unrelated to the Transak provider, fiat conversion, supported payment methods, mint behavior, or deferred lifecycle.
Developer verification of the project for browser or wallet trust systems is distinct from Lit Protocol ownership verification and ebook access gating.
Reporting the warning as a false positive and requesting developer verification does not revise any approved FAQ wording, including the existing scam explanation.
The operational trust-verification submission does not alter the About page's approved content or resolve its reward-delivery ambiguity.
Remediating an external scam warning does not change the SIWE authentication method, its user segment, or its required crypto flows.
The project-verification request has no effect on secondary-sale royalties, ERC-721C enforcement, founder allocation, commissions, or ticket rules.
Browser or wallet trust verification does not modify the ETH payment, exact-output swap, mint, or excess-refund behavior.
The false-positive report and developer verification request do not change the USDC wallet mint flow or its expected NFT outcome.
The project-verification page is unrelated to email or magic-link authentication and does not change dashboard access behavior.
The trust-warning remediation action does not entail any revision to the Mission page copy or its transparency statements.
